quote: I have often thought it would be a blessing if each human being were stricken blind and deaf for a few days at some time during his early adult life. Darkness would make him more appreciative of sight; silence would teach him the joys of sound.
source: Helen Keller, Three Days to See, part I, The Atlantic Monthly, January 1933

evidence.where: The American Foundation for the Blind’s Helen Keller Archive, which prints the essay as published in the Atlantic Monthly of January 1933, with its four numbered parts
evidence.locator: part I, before part II opens Perhaps I can best illustrate

reason: The keeper of Keller’s papers prints the Atlantic text, and the two sentences stand there in this wording inside part I of four. Keller has no line yet this year; the Atlantic page number was not seen, so none is given.
